chunks: Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Abdullah ibn Talha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a thief who entered upon a woman to steal her belongings. When he had gathered the clothes, his soul followed him, so he overpowered her and had intercourse with her. Her son stirred, so he (the thief) stood up and killed him with an axe that was with him. When he was finished, he carried the clothes and went to exit. She attacked him with the axe and killed him. His family came the next day seeking his blood. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Judge regarding this as I have described to you.'

He said: 'The guardians of the deceased, who are seeking his blood, are responsible for the wergild of the boy. The thief is responsible, from what he left, for four thousand dirhams, because he overpowered her and had intercourse with her, so he is an adulterer, and he is a debtor in his wealth. There is nothing upon her regarding her killing him.'
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever overpowers a woman to have illicit relations with her, and she kills him, then there is no wergild for him, nor retaliation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money ruling for a thief who rapes and is killed by the woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'gharamah' (debt) in Shia jurisprudence, where the thief's rape is treated as a financial liability against his estate rather than a capital crime requiring blood money. It highlights the legal distinction between the son's death, for which the thief's heirs pay, and the woman's act of killing him, which is exempt from retaliation (qisas) due to her right to defend her honor. The ruling underscores the principle that when a person commits multiple offenses, the specific nature of each determines the corresponding legal recompense.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Hafs, from Abdullah Bin Talha,

(The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> him<sup>asws</sup> about a male thief who entered upon a woman in order to steal her belongings. So when he gathered the clothes, he followed his soul, so he overcame her and fell upon her. So her son stirred, so he (the thief), stood up and killed him with an axe which was with him. So when he was free, he carried the clothes and gold in order to exit. She attacked him with the axe, so she killed him. So his family members came over in the morning seeking his blood. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> shall judge upon this just as it has been described to you’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His guardians, those who were seeking his blood are responsible for the wergild of the boy, and the thief is responsible with regards to what he has left (as legacy), four thousand Dirhams due to him having forced himself upon her chastity. It is adultery, and it’s fine is upon his wealth, and there is nothing upon her regarding her having killed him.
Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who forces himself upon a woman in order to be immoral with her, so she kills him, so there is no wergild for him, nor a retaliation’.
